bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: I never see it; I only wonder, in the lunch break while reading the rejection, whether the must-haves were fair and not about my age.
bundles.why: The blocking of age criteria sounds good, but I cannot see it, so I only care if the reason in my email matches a real requirement.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: When I read the rejection and see whether it quotes my 12 years of experience correctly, or got my jobs wrong.
bundles.why: If a machine misread my CV and nobody can correct it, that is exactly the unfairness I suspect; showing the working and allowing correction matters.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: At lunch, when I open the email and want to know which requirement I supposedly missed and whether a human confirmed it.
bundles.why: A named person confirming a written reason for 'missing' is the only thing that answers my fear that AI rejected me for my age.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Only if I were shortlisted; as a rejected candidate I never meet it.
bundles.why: It does not affect me now, as I was turned down, and asking for proof only from shortlisted people seems reasonable.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: On my phone at lunch, reading the email, in the first sentence, deciding in 3 minutes whether to reply with a complaint.
bundles.why: A specific reason with my own CV lines that I can check as true or false is the only thing that stops me going public; a generic reason makes me complain.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Never; it is only for the HR lead.
bundles.why: Totals without names do not help me, though it is good that it does not rank individuals.

proof_timing.why: Uploading degree certificates and referees for every application is a lot of effort and personal data for a job I may not get, so I would probably skip it; after shortlisting, with the reason stated, it is fair.
